questions.stem: Before right-knee surgery, the consent is correct but a whiteboard note lists the left knee. Who should perform the required site marking under current Joint Commission guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Any staff member who notices the discrepancy may mark the site after checking the consent because site marking does not need to remain linked to procedural accountability.","B":"The patient should mark the site alone because involvement of the practitioner could bias the verification process when conflicting documentation exists.","C":"An unlicensed assistant may mark the site independently as long as a nurse later checks the mark during the final time-out immediately before incision.","D":"The licensed practitioner accountable for the procedure should mark the site, involving the patient when possible; limited delegation is allowed under defined policy."}}
questions.rationale: Joint Commission guidance updated in 2026 states that the site is marked by the licensed practitioner ultimately accountable for the procedure and who will be present when it is performed. Limited delegation may occur under defined supervisory/collaborative circumstances, and the patient should be involved whenever possible.
questions.source_name: The Joint Commission — Universal Protocol: Site Marking
questions.source_detail: 2026 Joint Commission FAQ: accountable licensed practitioner marks the site; limited delegation is permitted in defined circumstances; patient involvement is expected when possible.

questions.stem: An emergency department has had several incidents involving aggressive visitors, especially when staff work alone in poorly visible hallways. Which prevention strategy best aligns with OSHA guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a violence-prevention program with hazard assessment, de-escalation training, reporting, security controls, and measures that reduce isolated work when feasible.","B":"Ask staff not to report threats that do not cause injury because documenting lower-level events increases administrative workload without improving prevention.","C":"Rely mainly on individual staff confidence because formal training, environmental design, security planning, and staffing practices do not materially affect violence risk.","D":"Encourage staff to approach escalating visitors alone so other patients are not alarmed and security is used only after an actual physical assault occurs."}}
questions.rationale: OSHA identifies working alone, poor environmental design, inadequate security, and lack of staff training and policies as healthcare workplace-violence risks. Recommended controls include a formal prevention program, worksite analysis, hazard controls, training to recognize and de-escalate violence, reporting, and security/environmental measures.
questions.source_detail: OSHA identifies working alone and inadequate security/training as risk factors and recommends comprehensive workplace-violence prevention programs with training and hazard controls.

questions.stem: A container of an unfamiliar cleaning chemical spills in a clinical work area and staff do not know its hazards. Which initial response is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue routine work around the spill until symptoms develop because a spill that appears small does not require hazard identification or protective measures.","B":"Stop the task, keep people away from the exposure area as appropriate, alert the facility response system, and use the SDS and trained spill procedures before cleanup.","C":"Clean the spill immediately with bare hands and paper towels because rapid removal is safer than waiting to identify the substance or obtain appropriate protective equipment.","D":"Evacuate the entire building for every chemical spill regardless of substance, quantity, ventilation, exposure risk, or the facility's hazardous-material response plan."}}
questions.rationale: OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard requires employees to have access to hazard information, labels, Safety Data Sheets, and protective procedures. Unknown chemical spills should be managed through the facility's trained hazardous-material/spill response, with exposure control based on the chemical and circumstances. Automatic building evacuation is not the correct response to every minor spill, and untrained cleanup is unsafe.
questions.source_name: OSHA — Hazard Communication and Hazardous Chemicals in Hospitals
questions.source_detail: OSHA requires hazard communication, SDS access, employee training and appropriate protective measures for hazardous chemicals; spill response depends on the substance and exposure conditions.

questions.stem: A nurse manager wants to improve a unit with low morale and inconsistent quality-improvement participation. Which leadership behavior best reflects a transformational approach?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Set all goals alone, discourage staff input, and use corrective discipline as the main method for obtaining compliance with unit expectations and improvement targets.","B":"Avoid setting a shared direction and allow each staff member to define independent priorities because leader involvement can reduce professional autonomy and creativity.","C":"Articulate a shared vision, invite staff ideas, develop team members, and connect quality-improvement work with meaningful patient and professional outcomes.","D":"Focus mainly on short-term rewards for task completion without mentoring, shared purpose, learning, or participation in how the unit improves care processes."}}
questions.rationale: Transformational leadership is characterized by a compelling shared purpose, development and empowerment of team members, support for learning and innovation, and alignment around better organizational and patient outcomes. Modern nurse-leader competency frameworks likewise emphasize leading people, influencing systems, collaboration, learning, and professional development.
questions.source_detail: AONL's contemporary nurse-leader competency framework emphasizes leading people, influencing systems, professional development, collaboration and organizational outcomes.

questions.stem: Two nurses disagree about how aggressively to mobilize a client who recently fell. Both have clinically relevant information, and the disagreement is beginning to disrupt the team. Which approach is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid discussing the disagreement so each nurse can follow a separate plan during their own shift, reducing interpersonal tension even if care becomes inconsistent.","B":"Have the more senior nurse make the decision without reviewing the other nurse's concerns because hierarchy is the preferred method for resolving informational conflict.","C":"Escalate immediately to formal disciplinary action against one nurse before attempting a structured discussion because unresolved clinical disagreement is misconduct.","D":"Use a structured collaborative discussion to share the concern and evidence, seek agreement, and create one patient-centered plan addressing mobility and fall risk."}}
questions.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS treats differing views about the care plan as informational conflict that should be resolved before it compromises quality or safety. Structured tools such as DESC, CUS, the Two-Challenge Rule, huddles, and collaborative discussion help teams focus on evidence, shared goals, and a mutually workable patient-centered plan.
questions.source_name: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS — Conflict in Teams and DESC
questions.source_detail: TeamSTEPPS recommends constructive conflict-resolution tools and collaboration to reach a safe, mutually acceptable solution centered on patient and team goals.
